# NT kernel-mode driver host: ntoskrnl and hal export surface

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_ntos_surface.py. Do not edit by hand. -->
<!-- Regenerate: python tools/gen_ntos_surface.py --repo . --out docs/status/DRIVERHOST-EXPORTS.md -->

The driver host (`src/kernel/nt/driver/`) loads a native x64 `.sys`, binds its
imports against the exports listed in `drvhost_exports.c`, and runs its
DriverEntry, PnP and IRP dispatch. A driver that imports a name that is not
listed as implemented here fails to load with `STATUS_PROCEDURE_NOT_FOUND`, and
DbgPrint names every unresolved import, so one attempt lists them all.

## Summary

- Ranked names in the manifest: 342
- Ranked and implemented: 171 (50.0%)
- Ranked and missing: 171
- Implemented exports in total: 233
- Implemented but not in the ranking: 62

Per tier (1 = needed by almost every driver, 4 = niche):

| Tier | Ranked | Implemented | Missing |
|-----:|-------:|------------:|--------:|
| 1 | 38 | 38 | 0 |
| 2 | 141 | 115 | 26 |
| 3 | 119 | 11 | 108 |
| 4 | 44 | 7 | 37 |

## Notes

- Scope: userspace-hosted model on the Linux guest (pthreads, mmap). The host
  is not yet linked into the personality kernel module.
- Calling convention: every driver-facing function and data export uses the
  Microsoft x64 ABI (`__attribute__((ms_abi))`, `DRVCALL` in `drvhost_types.h`).
- Data exports (`PsThreadType`, `IoFileObjectType`, ...) are object-type pointers
  and are referenced by drivers as `*PsThreadType`, as in the WDK.
- Import binding is by exact name within the module the driver names. Ordinal
  imports fail the load. Imports from modules other than ntoskrnl.exe and hal.dll
  fail the load.
- IRQL is tracked per thread. Misuse (for example waiting at DISPATCH_LEVEL with a
  timeout, or recursive acquisition of a spin lock) bugchecks the host and aborts.

## Layout confidence

The x64 structure layouts that drivers touch directly (`DRIVER_OBJECT`, `DEVICE_OBJECT`, `IRP`,
`IO_STACK_LOCATION`, `FILE_OBJECT`, `KDPC`, `KEVENT`, `FAST_MUTEX`, `KMUTANT`, `KSEMAPHORE`, `ERESOURCE`,
the lookaside lists and more) were first written from memory. They are now compared field by field with the
WDK definitions in Wine's headers (`third_party/wine/include`) by `make -C tests/kernel-drivers layout`;
the list of measured fields is `tests/kernel-drivers/layout/layout_list.h`. That comparison found and
fixed errors in `KDPC`, `DEVICE_OBJECT`, `FILE_OBJECT`, `IRP` and the `IO_STACK_LOCATION` parameter
blocks. A structure that is not in the list has not been compared. The first vendor-driver run is the
check of the rest.
